title: Between My Hands I Took...
text:
Between my hands I took

a tiny fistful of earth.

The land-wind was blowing.

The earth returned to earth.


Between your hands you hold me;

I am earth.

The wind airs

your fingers, long with centuries.


And the tiny fistful of sand

-grain by grain, grain by grain-

the great wind carries it away.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the poem's small scale and its movement from human touch back into elemental earth.

title: Naked They Have Fallen...
text:
Naked they have fallen,

the eleven chimes.


The speckled hens

peck at the trees' shadow,

and a swarm of bees

goes grumbling above.


Morning

has broken its necklace from the tower.


On the trunks, the cicadas scratch themselves.


Behind the garden fence,

slipping,

still,

your white parasol.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the clipped still-life of sound, shade, insects, and the white parasol.

title: The Wind Is a Dog Without an Owner...
text:
The wind is a dog without an owner,

licking the immense night.

The night has no sleep.

And man, among dreams, thinks.


And man dreams, sleeping,

that the wind is a dog without an owner,

howling stretched out at his feet

to lick his dream.


And still the hour has not struck.


The night has no sleep:

keep watch, sleepless one!
editorial_note: The translation keeps the recurring ownerless dog image and renders 'veladora' as the wakeful watcher.

title: The Star Counters
text:
I am tired.

I look at

this city

-any city-

where for twenty years I have lived.


Everything is the same.

A child

uselessly counts the stars

on the neighboring balcony.


I start as well...

But he goes faster: I cannot

catch up with him:

One, two, three, four,

five...


I cannot

catch up with him: One, two...

three...

four...

five...
editorial_note: The translation keeps the counting rhythm and the speaker's quiet inability to keep pace.

title: The Door, Open...
text:
The door, open.

She came quiet and soft.

Neither matter nor spirit. She brought

a slight leaning of a ship

and a morning light of clear day.


She was not rhythm, she was not harmony

nor color. The heart knows it,

but I could not say how she was,

because she is not form, nor can form contain her.


Tongue, mortal clay, inept chisel,

leave intact the flower of the concept

on this clear night of my wedding,


and sing gently, humbly,

the sensation, the shadow, the accident,

while she fills my whole soul.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the mystical arrival as something the heart knows but language cannot shape.
